newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, soymeal.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on exports, soymeal.

text.p: Bullish export data plus a strong rally in nearby soymeal tied to rumors China again was seeking the feed product boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"Good export numbers, they were all above expectations," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

USDA early Monday, in its weekly export inspections report, said U.S. soy inspected for export during the week ended December 12 totaled 36.236 million bushels, above trade estimates for 20 million to 25 million bushels.
Gains were limited by good crop weather in South America.
Weather conditions have been nearly ideal for the growing South American soybean crop amid only occasional concerns over a few pockets of dryness in Brazil and Argentina.

Soybean futures also found support from slow farmer selling, mostly firm cash basis markets and cold weather in the United States which suggested the amount of soymeal fed to the nation's livestock herd will increase.
Soybeans closed six to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with January up 7-1/4 at $7.11-1/2. March was up 6-1/4 at $7.07.
Futures punched through first resistance in January, noted by technical traders at $7.06-1/2 per bushel as well as second resistance at $7.11-1/4. The session high for January was $7.12.
First support was pegged by traders at $7.02 a bushel and second support at $6.97-1/2. The session low was $7.03-1/2.
Chartists also reported the four- and 20-day moving averages for the January contract were giving off bearish signals after the close Friday.
Tenco Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of March and bought two million January and Refco Inc bought 2.5 million March but sold 1.5 million January, traders said.
ADM Investor Services and Cargill Inc bull spread three million bushels of January/March, the traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 50,000 contracts, above the 40,956 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Refco Inc bought 200 January $7.00 puts at 3-3/4 cents, Tenco Inc bought 200 January $7.00 puts at 2-3/4 and Cargill Investor Services sold 200 July $7.00 puts at 33-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 16,430 traded Friday.
